title: Recycling & the Bin Lorry
strapline: The bin lorry rumbles up the road, the crew hop off, and all our sorted rubbish is whisked away to be made into something new.
intent: The bin lorry and its crew are among the most fascinating community helpers to young children, and exploring them builds knowledge of the people whose everyday work keeps our streets clean.
Sorting waste into the right bins — paper, plastic, glass, food — is genuine, purposeful mathematics: classifying, matching and grouping by material and rule.
Children learn real, important knowledge about caring for the world — why we recycle, what happens to our rubbish, how looking after the planet is everyone's job.
Loading, pushing, lifting and driving the lorry is satisfying gross-motor play with a clear real-world purpose.
Working the round as a crew — collecting, sorting, tipping — grows cooperation, sequence and the language of a real job.
Vocabulary and community knowledge grow — recycle, sort, bin, collect, waste, reuse, material, environment.
implementation: Set up recycling stations with clearly labelled bins and a collection of clean junk, and a ride-on or role-play bin lorry to work the round outdoors.
Take a role in the round — the driver, a resident putting bins out — so children collect, sort and tip as a working crew.
Model the sorting talk: 'This one's a plastic bottle and this is cardboard — which bin does each belong in? How do you know?'
Bring in maths through the play — sort by material, count and tally what's collected, compare which bin is fullest, group by colour and type.
Weave in real knowledge about caring for the world — why we recycle, what our rubbish becomes, reusing junk in the making area rather than binning it.
Extend into junk modelling so 'waste' is genuinely reused, and talk about your setting's own real recycling and the bin day on your street.
key_questions: This one's a plastic bottle and this is cardboard — which bin does each belong in?
How do you know which bin it goes in?
Which bin is the fullest — how could we check?
What happens to our rubbish after the crew takes it away?
How could we reuse this instead of binning it?
